# Parameter matrix — what survives each conversion

Generated 2026-09-25 from the source, by `tools/parameter_matrix.py`.



Both halves come from the **AST**, never from a text search — a comment
mentioning `filter_cutoff` must not count as reading it, which is a mistake
this project has already made in a test.

    SET by a reader      an `Assign` to `<obj>.field`; `field=` passed as a
                         keyword to ANY call (the MPC reader splats a
                         20-key `dict(...)` into its constructor); a literal
                         `setattr`; or the field's name appearing inside a
                         dict, list, tuple or set — a DISPATCH TABLE, which is
                         how the AKAI reader selects a pan routing. A name in
                         a comment or a docstring is none of those.
    READ by a writer     an attribute `Load` of `.field`, or
                         `getattr(obj, 'field')` with a literal name
    either side          a `@property` that proxies onto a field counts as
                         that field -- `env_attack` is `amp_env`. The alias
                         map is read from `models/common.py`, not listed here

### ⚠ What this scan CANNOT see, stated because a scan's fit is not coverage

* **A field consumed through a helper.** If a writer passes a whole voice to a
  function in `models/common.py` and that function reads the field, the read
  happens outside the writer's module and this reports it as dropped.
* **`getattr` with a computed name.** Only literal names are counted.
* **Whether the value is CORRECT.** A cell says the field is carried from the
  reader to the writer, not that the conversion is faithful, calibrated or
  hardware-confirmed. `docs/RESOLUTION_NOTES.md` is where that lives.
* **A field only ever MUTATED through a method** was invisible until
  2026-09-25 (`voice.mod_routings.append(...)` has no `Store` in it at all).
  Now counted for `append`/`extend`/`insert`/`update`/`add` on a model-field
  attribute, and for `obj.field[k] = v`. Any other mutation route is still
  unseen.
* **A read for a DECISION rather than for EMISSION.** ⚠ Found 2026-09-25 by
  checking a surprising cell: `lfo1_delay` shows as read by the KRZ writer,
  but the only use is a voice-FUSION compatibility test (`getattr(a, name) !=
  getattr(b, name)` — two voices with different LFO delays must not merge).
  The K2000's LFO page has no delay field at all, so nothing is emitted. A `+`
  means the writer's module touches the field; confirm what it does with it
  before quoting a cell as coverage.
* **Conditional writes.** A field written only under some branch reads the
  same here as one written always.

So a `+` means *"this path can carry it"*, and a `-` means *"nothing in the
writer's own module reads it"*. Treat a surprising `-` as a place to look, not
as a proven gap — that is the same standing as any other scan in this repo.

⚠ **The generator is not in the repository.** `.gitignore` excludes `tools/`
and `tests/`, so this file ships and `tools/parameter_matrix.py` does not, and
a clone cannot regenerate or check it. That is the same open issue already
recorded for `tools/firmware_sim_contract.py`; until it is settled, treat a
published copy of this table as of its stated date rather than as current.

#### How each surprising cell was checked before publishing

Four scan rules were wrong in a way the totals could not show, and each was
found by asking a question with a known answer rather than by reading output:

* the constructor whitelist missed the MPC reader's `dict(...)` splat, so the
  MPC path looked as if it dropped `filter_cutoff`;
* no alias map meant `amp_env` and `filter_env` looked dropped on every path,
  because every reader and writer names the stages, never the object;
* no dispatch-table rule meant the AKAI pan routings wired the same day looked
  unset — `lfo1_to_pan` passed anyway, from an unrelated assignment, which is
  what a single positive probe would have rested on;
* the negative control is the Roland and Ensoniq readers, which must set
  mapping fields only. They set 13 and 9 fields, all of them mapping — which
  is the claim `tests/test_source_target_restriction.py` makes in prose,
  arrived at independently here.

### Legend

| | |
|---|---|
| **+** | the reader sets it **and** the writer reads it — this pair can carry it |
| **–** | the reader sets it, the writer's module does not read it — **dropped here** |
| *(blank)* | the reader never sets it — nothing to carry |
| **n/a** | identity pair, or a pair this converter refuses |

⚠ **Ensoniq/Roland sources convert to e4b and krz only** — every other target is refused with a non-zero exit, in ordinary conversion as well as with `--firmware-sim`, because nothing outside this project could check the result. Those cells read `n/a` rather than `–`.
